Summary of 'sroc' objects

summary.sroc.Rd

Summarize the results of reitsma.sroc or hattori.tsroc (for each time point): convergence of the optimizer, the log-likelihood, the estimates of \((\mu_1, \mu_2, \tau_1, \tau_2, \rho)\) with standard errors (SE) and confidence intervals, the summary sensitivity, specificity, and SAUC, and all the estimates (par.all).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'sroc'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted object returned by the function reitsma.sroc or hattori.tsroc.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "summary.sroc": a list with

call

The call of the fitting function (if recorded).

time.dependent

TRUE for the results of hattori.tsroc.

ci.level

The confidence level.

fits

A list with one element for each fit (time point), each a list of ok, K (number of studies), conv, message, logLik, coef (matrix of the estimates, SEs, and confidence limits), sauc, sens, spec (estimate and confidence limits), and par.all.

It is printed by print.summary.sroc.

Details

The SEs are the square roots of the diagonal elements of var.ml (the inverse of the numerical Hessian matrix of the negative log-likelihood). The confidence intervals are the Wald intervals of \(\mu_1\) and \(\mu_2\), of \(\log\tau_1\) and \(\log\tau_2\), and of \(\mathrm{atanh}(\rho)\) (Fisher's z), back-transformed; so they stay within the parameter space. The confidence level is ci.level used in the fitting function (0.95 by default).

See also

print.sroc, print.summary.sroc, plot.sroc

Examples

data(IVD)
fit <- reitsma.sroc(TP = TP, FN = FN, FP = FP, TN = TN, data = IVD)
summary(fit)
#> SROC curve: bivariate random-effects model (Reitsma et al., 2005)
#> Publication bias is not considered
#> 
#> Call:
#> reitsma.sroc(TP = TP, FN = FN, FP = FP, TN = TN, data = IVD)
#> 
#> ============================================================
#> Results
#> ============================================================
#> Number of studies: 33
#> Convergence:       yes (relative convergence (4))
#> Log-likelihood:    -31.076
#> 
#> Parameters (tau1, tau2: between-study SDs; rho: correlation)
#> ------------------------------------------------------------
#>      Estimate    SE          95% CI
#> mu1     1.484 0.177  [1.136, 1.832]
#> mu2     1.824 0.154  [1.522, 2.125]
#> tau1    0.597 0.175  [0.336, 1.062]
#> tau2    0.826 0.117  [0.626, 1.090]
#> rho    -0.424 0.236 [-0.769, 0.111]
#> 
#> Summary measures
#> ------------------------------------------------------------
#>             Estimate         95% CI
#> Sensitivity    0.815 [0.757, 0.862]
#> Specificity    0.861 [0.821, 0.893]
#> SAUC           0.874 [0.806, 0.920]
#> 
#> All estimates (par.all)
#> ------------------------------------------------------------
#>    mu1    mu2 tau1^2 tau2^2  tau12   sauc   sens   spec 
#>  1.484  1.824  0.357  0.683 -0.209  0.874  0.815  0.861 
#> 

## the coefficient table as a matrix
s <- summary(fit)
s$fits[[1]]$coef
#>        Estimate        SE      lower     upper
#> mu1   1.4839917 0.1774776  1.1361421 1.8318413
#> mu2   1.8236493 0.1538733  1.5220632 2.1252355
#> tau1  0.5974413 0.1753902  0.3360539 1.0621394
#> tau2  0.8261895 0.1167857  0.6262653 1.0899360
#> rho  -0.4244263 0.2363535 -0.7690938 0.1114831
